purpose: One record per ship: where each number in the fleet manifest comes from (citation, URL, license, the exact table/section it would be read from) and how far that provenance was actually checked in this environment. The registry exists so that a reader can re-derive every manifest digit from the named source instead of trusting the manifest, and so that 'verified' means one specific thing (the source was re-read here) rather than a mood.
environment_limit: This execution environment has no outbound network (verified 2026-11-13 by attempting the workshop URLs; the sandbox blocks egress). No official IGES / offset file and no workshop page could be re-fetched, so every entry is retrieval=offline_recollection with verified=false, and the verification that is reported is arithmetic (the cited displacement vs the cited Cb*L*B*T), not a source re-read.
license_note: The benchmark particulars are published for research use by the workshop organisers; none of them ships an explicit OSI licence file, so the licence column states what the publication actually grants (research use of published data) rather than inventing a licence name. Nothing here is redistributed: the repository stores numbers and 4-decimal citations, not the organisers' files.

sources.citation: Numerical Ship Hydrodynamics: An Assessment of the Gothenburg 2010 Workshop (eds. Larsson, Stern, Visonneau), Springer 2014 — KCS (MOERI/KRISO 3600 TEU container ship) test case
sources.license: published workshop benchmark data, research use
sources.locator: KCS test-case particulars (Lpp, B, T, Cb, Cm, LCB, displacement volume)
sources.note: Lpp = 230.0 m, B = 32.2 m, T = 10.8 m, Cb = 0.651, Cm = 0.971, LCB = -1.48 % Lpp, grad = 52030 m^3 are the workshop-standard digits; the triple reproduces the cited volume to 0.08 %.

sources.citation: SIMMAN 2008 / SIMMAN 2014 workshop series (eds. Stern, Agdrup) — MOERI KVLCC2 tanker test case
sources.license: published workshop benchmark data, research use
sources.locator: KVLCC2 test-case particulars (Lpp 320.0 m, B 58.0 m, T 20.8 m, Cb 0.8098, Cm 0.9956, LCB +3.48 % Lpp, grad 312622 m^3)
sources.note: Cb 0.8098 is the value that makes Cb*L*B*T reproduce the published grad 312622 m^3 (agreement 1e-4), which is why the two digits corroborate each other rather than being independent.

sources.citation: El Moctar, O., Shigunov, V., Zorn, T. (2012) Duisburg Test Case: Post-Panamax Container Ship for Benchmarking. Ship Technology Research 59(3), 50-64
sources.locator: DTC main particulars table (Lpp 355.0 m, B 51.0 m, T 14.5 m, Cb 0.661, grad 173467 m^3)
sources.note: This entry corrects the record: the manifest previously carried B = 45.8 m, which makes Cb*L*B*T = 155834 m^3, i.e. 11.3 % away from the cited 173467 m^3. The quadruple (355.0, 51.0, 14.5, 0.661) reproduces 173467 m^3 to 0.0005 % and gives L/B = 6.96, B/T = 3.52 — a post-Panamax container ship; the G6b gate now rejects the old quadruple, and the negative control mis_transcribed_particulars keeps that regression pinned.
